run_2008_separate_process_profile.provenance_qualification: Separate-process production-factory invocation completed in 0.742s without concurrent browser fanout; negative evidence showing isolated execution does not reproduce or explain the live HTTP worker reload timeout.

run_2039_sampled_browser_fanout.provenance_qualification: In the 20:39 sampled run, the initial mount completed as full bff_composed (while the 20:00 initial mount returned partial_composition), and the reload timed out at 3.0s with empty operator_home and runtime_health. Access-log timestamps record completion times without request-ID linkage across overlapping browser fanout requests, and 50Hz py-spy stack samples do not carry HTTP request IDs; therefore synchronous downstream_health_monitor SQLite/JSON/socket work on the serial owner-read critical path is documented as a concrete contributor alongside serial owner waterfalls and cross-wave worker contention rather than sole-cause proof.

proven_root_causes.cause: get_operator_health_status executed all five health groups and DomainGovernancePort.list_governance_review_queue_items' three owner reads (approval_records, list_deployment_plans, list_evolution_decisions) strictly serially, and get_human_inbox executed its persona/capital owner reads (list_personas, list_bindings, list_capital_pools) in a second serial waterfall after health completed. Live 50Hz py-spy sampling on 2026-10-21T20:39Z (Thread 86, 2.78s segment) showed serial owner reads combined with synchronous socket.readinto (0.84s), JSON raw_decode (0.82s), and downstream_health_monitor SQLite commit work (0.56s commit / 0.84s total monitor work) contributing to the 3.0s PANTHEON_BFF_COCKPIT_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS budget exhaustion before Section 1 (runtime_health) could complete on reload. Additionally, _resolve_group collapsed deadline exhaustion / pending future timeout and RuntimeError into identical error surfaces.
proven_root_causes.repair: Execute the independent health group reads and governance/cockpit owner read warmers concurrently within request_read_scope on a bounded worker pool while bounding group wait to the remaining management_read_deadline with headroom, and distinguish read_timeout (source: management_read_timeout, reason: read_timeout) from read_error (source: error, reason: read_error) in _resolve_group and health_status surface metadata.

proven_root_causes.cause: cached_owner_call checked and populated request_read_cache without synchronization, so concurrent threads sharing a request_read_scope via copy_context().run could race or duplicate identical owner reads; and fallback locking when request_read_cache was set to a plain dict must not share a single non-reentrant lock across nested cached_owner_call keys or retain plain-dict request caches in a module-global registry.
proven_root_causes.repair: Add per-key RLock synchronization on _RequestReadCache._key_locks and plain-dict request_read_cache instances (via an in-cache private non-tuple sentinel key with zero cross-request retention) in cached_owner_call and lock-protected eviction in evict_request_read_keys so distinct or nested owner reads never deadlock while identical in-flight owner keys within the same request are deduplicated.

proven_root_causes.cause: run_management_read did not propagate its outer deadline to inner contributor reads (_StoreTimeoutProxy, _bounded_persona_readiness_rows) or subsequent cockpit sections, allowing timed-out worker threads to continue spawning fresh 3.0s contributor reads across the reload window.
proven_root_causes.repair: Propagate management_read_deadline via ContextVar in run_management_read and cap _StoreTimeoutProxy, _bounded_persona_readiness_rows, and post-deadline cockpit sections to remaining_management_read_budget.

proven_root_causes.cause: _bounded_get_human_inbox mutated self._resolve_store on the shared ManagementService instance across concurrent cockpit and human-inbox requests and declared synchronous GET handlers as async def without await.
proven_root_causes.repair: Bind _StoreTimeoutProxy per-request via _MANAGEMENT_STORE_OVERRIDE ContextVar instead of mutating self._resolve_store on ManagementService, and declare synchronous GET route handlers as def so FastAPI runs them on its threadpool.
